title: ARY, ERY or ORY?
kidRule: Three endings sound almost the same: A-R-Y as in DICTIONARY, E-R-Y as in GALLERY, and O-R-Y as in FACTORY. The vowel is hard to hear, so say the word slowly in your spelling voice and remember which vowel it uses!
hint: Listen to the end of this word. One vowel is hard to hear. Is it an A, an E, or an O?
reminder: This ending is A-R-Y, E-R-Y or O-R-Y. A cousin word can help: HISTORIC shows the O in HISTORY, and MACHINE keeps its E in MACHINERY.

check.question: Why is the ending of FACTORY tricky to spell?
check.correctAnswer: Because A-R-Y, E-R-Y and O-R-Y sound almost the same, so I must remember that this word uses O!
distractors: Because the Y at the end is silent
Because every word for a building ends with O-R-Y

words.def: A book or website that lists words in ABC order and tells what they mean.
words.sent: I looked up the new word in my dictionary.
words.story: Noah Webster worked for more than 20 years on his American dictionary of 1828, which explained about 70,000 words!
words.card: I pre*dict* the puppy will chew my *dictionary* and swallow all the words!

words.def: A building where people and machines make lots of things.
words.sent: My uncle works at a factory that makes bicycles.
words.story: The Crayola factory in Pennsylvania makes about 12 million crayons every single day!
words.card: The clowns *act* silly at the pie *factory* and come out covered in cream!

words.def: A room or building where people go to look at art.
words.sent: Our class paintings were hung in the school gallery.
words.story: The Louvre in Paris is the most visited art museum in the world, and it is the home of the famous Mona Lisa!
words.card: We *all* giggled when a pigeon strolled into the *gallery* to look at the art!

words.def: Everything that happened in the past, and the study of it.
words.sent: We learned about the history of our town at the museum.
words.story: The word comes from the Greek 'historia', which meant finding things out by asking questions!
words.card: The *history* of my sock is a sad *story*: the dog ate its twin!

words.def: Not real; only in your mind or in a story.
words.sent: My little brother has an imaginary friend named Bop.
words.story: The equator is an imaginary line around the middle of the Earth. Nobody can see it, but it is drawn on every globe!
words.card: My *imaginary* dragon does *magi*c tricks with marshmallows!

words.def: Machines, or the moving parts inside a machine.
words.sent: The farm machinery rumbled across the field.
words.story: The word 'machine' comes from the Greek 'mechane', which meant a clever device!
words.card: The *machine* went BOING, and all the *machinery* started juggling jelly!

words.def: Something that is found or learned for the very first time.
words.sent: The discovery of a dinosaur egg made the scientists cheer.
words.story: The discovery of the Rosetta Stone in Egypt in 1799 helped people work out how to read ancient Egyptian picture writing!
words.card: I looked under the *cover* and made a *discovery*: the cat had hidden nine socks!

words.def: An area of land that belongs to a person, an animal, or a country.
words.sent: The robin sings to tell other birds that this is its territory.
words.story: Wolves howl to tell other wolf packs to stay out of their territory!
words.card: The *terri*er guards his *territory*: one sofa cushion and half a sock!

words.def: All the words that a person knows and uses.
words.sent: Reading lots of books helps your vocabulary grow.
words.story: A border collie named Chaser had an amazing vocabulary: she learned the names of more than 1,000 toys!
words.card: The taxi *cab* driver has a huge *vocabulary*, but his parrot only says 'Beep!'

words.def: A room where scientists do experiments and tests.
words.sent: The scientist mixed two liquids in her laboratory.
words.story: The International Space Station is a laboratory that flies around the Earth about 16 times every day!
words.card: It took hard *labor* to clean the *laboratory* after the slime bubbled over!
